hints: Focus on what makes structural isomers the same, they must have exactly the same molecular formula but a different arrangement.
Count every carbon in Q by counting each line end and each junction, each one is a carbon in a skeletal formula.
Count the carbons in each option the same way and keep the one with the same total as Q but with branching in a different place.
walkthrough:
**Find the formula of Q**

Great start, remember in skeletal formulas every end of a line and every bend is a carbon. Count them carefully for Q.

$$\text{Q = 7 chain carbons + 3 branch carbons = 10 carbons}$$
So Q is $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{22}$, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$, or 2,3,5-trimethylheptane.

**Count carbons in the options**

Now do the same counting trick for A to D. This is where most students rush, so take it slowly.

$$\text{A = 11 carbons, B = 11 carbons, C = 11 carbons, D = 10 carbons}$$
Only one option has the same number of carbons as Q. All alkanes follow $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n+2}$, so same carbon number means same molecular formula.

**Check for structural isomer**

A structural isomer must have the same formula, $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{22}$, but different connectivity. Option D is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}[\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2]\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

It has 10 carbons like Q, but the branches are arranged differently, a 3-isopropyl group on heptane instead of three methyl groups. That is exactly a structural isomer.

options.A: Incorrect. Counting ends and junctions gives 11 carbons, so about C11H24. It has one carbon too many to be an isomer of Q (C10H22). It is easy to miscount the isopropyl branch on the left.
options.B: Incorrect. The main chain is longer here with an ethyl branch and a methyl branch, giving 11 carbons in total. So its formula is C11H24, not C10H22. It looks similar to Q but fails the same-formula test.
options.C: Incorrect. This also totals 11 carbons with its isopropyl branch plus the longer chain. Its formula is C11H24, so it cannot be a structural isomer of the C10 molecule Q.
options.D: Correct. Counting gives 7 carbons in the longest chain plus 3 carbons in the isopropyl substituent, total 10 carbons. Its formula is C10H22, same as Q, but the connectivity is different, so it is a true structural isomer.
